A graph here is combinatorial, with no position until a layout gives it one,
which is [notebook 02](02-layouts.qmd)'s subject. Getting one in while keeping
its attributes intact is the hard part.

Two innocuous column names, `density` and `max_load`, send the importer down its
geospatial branch, because it matches latitude and longitude by the bare
substrings `y` and `x`: it builds a globe and posts the node identifiers to a
geocoder. The layout that runs on import zeroes every edge attribute it just
read, and an edge list cannot express an isolated node, so one of three hundred
quietly fails to arrive.
